newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Government should act to cool property prices - Hang Seng Bank vice chairman.
newsitem.headline: Government should act to cool property prices - Hang Seng Bank vice chairman.

text.p: The Hong Kong government should take measures now to cool rising property prices before a bubble is created, Alexander Au, vice chairman of Hang Seng Bank Ltd, said on Tuesday.

"I feel that speculative activities are now so rife that if we don't take some measures now we will be creating a bubble. Some measures should be taken now," Au told reporters after a ceremony in Kowloon to mark the opening of the bank's 146th branch in the territory.
"Obviously for the longer term we should aim to achieve equilibrium between supply and demand and of course that will take a bit of time to be achieved," Au said.

Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has expressed concern over the rampant speculation in the residential property market and has appointed C.Y. Leung, a member of his Executive Council, to study the issue.

Leung, also a property surveyor, said on Saturday he had completed a report outlining ideas to curb speculation. He gave no details of his proposals but said they would not affect long-term investors or genuine home buyers.
Tung and his administration assume office at midnight on June 30 when Hong Kong reverts to China after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Au declined to speculate on what measures the new government would take to stabilise property prices.
"Obviously I think we should wait (for the) announcement from the government," he said.
Hong Kong banks are heavily involved in mortgage lending.
Hang Seng Bank, one of the largest mortgage lenders, had about one-third of its lending portfolio in mortgage loans at the end of last year.
Au said he was not worried about possible adverse effects on the bank's business once the government introduces new measures on property.
"I don't think one should put banks' interest in the first place," he said. "I think we should look at the interest of the community as a whole. What is good for Hong Kong is good for the banks."

On Monday, outgoing colonial Governor Chris Patten warned that speculation in the booming property market would be a serious matter for the post-handover government and solutions would require a delicate touch,
"I don't want to say that things are getting out of control but I do agree that it is going to be a serious issue for the (post-handover) government to tackle," Patten told reporters.

"While you want to damp down speculation and any excessive increase in prices, you don't want to do anything which would damage the property market or investors' confidence in the medium and long term. So it is a difficult balance to strike."
